hero.title: Rapa Nui Park
hero.subtitle: The world’s first full-scale Ahu Tongariki inspired monument outside Easter Island.
hero.imageAlt: Visualisation of fifteen Moai statues on a monumental stone platform

slogan.description: Rapa Nui Park is a concept for creating a full-scale reconstruction in Poland of one of the world’s most recognisable archaeological ensembles. The project brings together education, culture, tourism and respect for Rapa Nui heritage.
slogan.imageAlt: Moai facing the panorama of Bystrzyca Kłodzka at sunset

project.title: A place where architectural scale meets education, landscape and cultural memory.
project.body: Rapa Nui Park is a concept for creating in Poland a full-scale reconstruction of Ahu Tongariki, one of the world’s most recognisable archaeological ensembles from Rapa Nui. The plan envisages 15 Moai arranged in a composition inspired by the original, with respect for the cultural heritage of Easter Island.

iorana.title: IORANA MOAI
iorana.intro: This part of the project is conceived as a tribute to the makers of the Moai and to the heritage of Rapa Nui. Its purpose is to share knowledge, invite deeper engagement with the story of Ahu Tongariki and build a thoughtful bridge between Europe and Easter Island.
iorana.imageAlt: Museum-style visualisation of Rano Raraku with an unfinished Moai held in the rock
iorana.imageBody: The great unfinished Moai in the slopes of Rano Raraku speaks of ambition, technical mastery and the spiritual dimension of the work of the island’s early inhabitants. Here, the visualisation serves reflection, education and a respectful invitation to discover the authentic history of Rapa Nui.
themes: A story of ancestral knowledge, stone craft and Rano Raraku as the birthplace of many statues.
An educational perspective grounded in respect for research, documentation and the authentic history of Ahu complexes.
The European concept is intended to bring Rapa Nui heritage to a wider audience and deepen curiosity about its sources.
iorana.dialogueBody: “IORANA MOAI” does not treat Rapa Nui culture as decoration. It is an invitation to encounter its history, achievements and place in world heritage with care, and with respect for the community whose memory and traditions stand behind this story.

statues.imageAlt: Architectural detail of the Moai alignment
statues.imageCaption: A sequence of fifteen figures read as a horizontal line in the landscape.
statues.title: Statue layout – a faithful copy from Rapa Nui
statues.intro: The planned composition is based on the clear axis of the Ahu platform, a sequence of fifteen figures and the characteristic rhythm known from the 1995 reconstruction of Ahu Tongariki.

functions.title: A programme designed as a coherent cultural and tourism destination.
functions.intro: The functions are shaped around longer visits, education, visitor services and the creation of new value for the region.
items: A monumental stone platform axis with fifteen statues.
Programmes on Rapa Nui heritage, archaeology and cultural preservation.
Temporary exhibitions, models, multimedia and the story of the reconstruction process.
Guest facilities rooted in the offer of the region.
A dialogue with the Kłodzko Valley landscape and the panorama of Bystrzyca.
Intimate concerts, talks, lectures and partnership programmes.

scale.title: Feel the scale
scale.subtitle: Stand before Ahu Tongariki and see how small a person becomes beside the monumental guardians of Rapa Nui.
scale.intro: Numbers describe height. Only the presence of a person truly reveals the monumentality of Ahu Tongariki.
scale.imageAlt: Ahu Tongariki visualisation showing the scale of the statues beside visitors
scale.closing: This will not be an exhibition viewed from a distance. It will be a place where people stop and feel their own scale.

night.title: NIGHTS OF AHU TONGARIKI
night.subtitle: When stone awakens to life.
night.body:
As the sun sets, Ahu Tongariki reveals a second identity.

The monumental silhouettes of the Moai emerge from darkness through carefully designed illumination, creating a space of silence, reflection and awe.

Evening light presentations, night viewing sessions, astronomy encounters and intimate cultural events turn each night into a distinct experience.
night.imageAlt: Night illumination of fifteen Moai statues on the Ahu Tongariki platform
night.panelTitle: Light that draws history from stone.
night.panelBody: The lighting is intended to guide the eye across facial features, stone texture and the rhythm of the entire platform, creating an experience that is calm, dignified and far removed from amusement-park spectacle.
cards: A daily light experience after sunset, emphasising the monumental presence of the statues.
A quiet zone for contemplation and observation of the Bystrzyca Kłodzka panorama.
Evenings with telescopes, sky observation and the Milky Way.
Acoustic music, historical narration, educational meetings and cultural gatherings.
night.finalWhite: From the first rays of sun to a night illuminated by stars.
night.finalGold: Ahu Tongariki reveals its beauty anew at every hour of the day.

governmentPartnership.title: A local government open to an extraordinary vision
paragraphs: The Rapa Nui Park project has drawn the interest of the local government of Bystrzyca Kłodzka, which recognises its potential as an exceptional tourist, cultural and educational attraction.

The Mayor of Bystrzyca Kłodzka, Renata Surma, together with the Bystrzyca Kłodzka Municipal Council, expressed openness to further dialogue on developing the project, promoting the region, and actions that could help strengthen the municipality's tourist appeal.

The project envisages the creation of a place with a truly distinctive character, capable of supporting the promotion of the Kłodzko Valley, the development of local entrepreneurship, and the building of the region's recognisability in Poland and beyond.

One of the project's long-term goals remains the development of international cooperation and the building of partnership relations with representatives of Rapa Nui, based on mutual respect for cultural heritage, education and the exchange of experience.

hero.title: Rapa Nui Park in winter
hero.claim: A place unlike any other on Earth
hero.subclaim: Where snow meets the guardians of the Pacific.
hero.disclaimer: A concept for the future winter chapter of Rapa Nui Park.
hero.imageAlt: A vision of Ahu Tongariki with fifteen Moai in the winter landscape of Rapa Nui Park.

twoWorlds.title: Two distant worlds. One extraordinary encounter.
paragraphs: Rapa Nui evokes the ocean, volcanic earth and the monumental silhouettes of the Moai. At Rapa Nui Park, that history gains a new European perspective.
In winter, dark stone, white snow, light and silence create a landscape that cannot be mistaken for anywhere else.
twoWorlds.note: The winter setting is not an attempt to recreate the climate of the original island. It is a deliberate meeting of Rapa Nui heritage with the landscape of Central Europe.
twoWorlds.imageAlt: A winter vision of Moai in the European landscape of the Kłodzko Valley.

comparison.title: One place. Two completely different experiences.
comparison.body: In summer, the space opens to light, greenery and distant panoramas. In winter, silence, snow and low light transform its character, revealing the monumentality of the Moai in a new way.
comparison.sliderLabel: A comparison of the summer and winter vision of Rapa Nui Park
comparison.summerAlt: Summer vision of Rapa Nui Park with the Moai platform.
comparison.winterAlt: Winter vision of Rapa Nui Park with the full Moai alignment.

story.kicker: THREE WINTER FACES OF THE PARK
story.title: The winter landscape as part of the experience

items.title: The Silence of the Guardians
items.body: Snow softens the space. Monumental silhouettes, wind and silence remain. A winter morning will reveal Ahu Tongariki in its most austere and contemplative form.
items.alt: Morning winter vision of the full fifteen-Moai alignment.

items.title: Light after dusk
items.body: Warm light will bring the faces of the Moai out of the winter half-darkness, while snow reflects the illumination and visually expands the entire space.
items.alt: Winter vision of Moai with warm illumination after dusk.

items.title: First light on snow
items.body: The first winter morning reveals the texture of stone and the stillness of the landscape. Snow reflects the warm light, making the Moai appear as calm silhouettes emerging from white silence.
items.alt: First winter morning light on snow-covered Moai.

times.title: From first light to winter night
times.body: The same landscape changes its character with light, weather and time of day.

items.label: WINTER MORNING
items.title: First light on snow
items.description: Fresh snow, low sun and delicate mist create a bright, focused opening to the morning visit.
items.alt: Winter morning at Rapa Nui Park.

items.label: BLUE HOUR
items.title: Deep sky and first lights
items.description: Cool snow and the first illumination reveal details of the Moai without turning the scene into spectacle.
items.alt: Blue hour in the winter vision of Rapa Nui Park.

items.label: NIGHT ILLUMINATION
items.title: Light, stone and winter silence
items.description: Warm light on Moai faces and snow reflecting the illumination create a deep, museum-like atmosphere.
items.alt: Night winter illumination of Moai at Rapa Nui Park.

experiences.title: The winter experience of Rapa Nui Park
experiences.intro: The winter landscape is not merely a backdrop. It becomes an integral part of the future visitor experience.

items.title: Winter viewing route
items.body: A planned route through key viewpoints for quiet discovery of the winter panorama of Ahu Tongariki.

items.title: Winter Nights of Ahu Tongariki
items.body: A special winter edition of illumination where light, snow and monumental Moai silhouettes form one calm spectacle.

items.title: Monumental landscape photography
items.body: Designed viewpoints will support photography of the Moai, the regional panorama and the distinctive winter light.

items.title: Warm resting space
items.body: A future rest area with views of the Ahu, hot drinks and an intimate educational display.

items.title: A story of two landscapes
items.body: An educational programme connecting Rapa Nui culture with the European setting of the park.

potential.title: An attraction that does not end with the season
paragraphs: The winter landscape is not a limitation of the project, but one of its most distinctive strengths. Rapa Nui Park can change with the seasons, offering visitors a different experience in summer, autumn, winter and spring.
The winter chapter strengthens the photographic, event and promotional potential of the project and helps build recognition as a year-round destination.

final.title:
In winter, the guardians
do not fall asleep.
final.body: They reveal their most extraordinary face.
final.cta: DISCOVER THE NIGHTS OF AHU TONGARIKI
final.imageAlt: Side winter view of the snow-covered Moai alignment at Rapa Nui Park.

awakening.title: Moai Awakening
awakening.subtitle: The day when stone regains memory.
awakening.lead: Moai Awakening is the narrative layer of RapaNuiPark: light, silence, traces and story guide visitors through the meaning of the guardians, not through a simple list of attractions.
awakening.rareLine: A moment of focus, not a show.
awakening.scrollAria: Scroll to the Moai Awakening story
awakening.heroAlt: Monumental RapaNuiPark Moai with a subtle eye-opening animation.

manifest.title: When the eyes of the Moai are open, the Park becomes more than a place to visit.
manifest.body: This section tells of a symbolic moment in which the guardians gaze gives order to the whole space. Every part of the Park can then become part of a larger story: about stone, ocean, memory, walking and responsibility toward the heritage of Rapa Nui.
manifest.freeRule: The Awakening does not need excess effects. Its power lies in the rhythm of passage: from the first gaze, through traces in the landscape, to evening light.

moments.title: The Park speaks through small signs.
moments.body: Instead of multiplying activities, the section builds rhythm: light, pause, sign, short story, moving onward. It is a calm dramaturgy of place, where every scene has meaning and does not need to be loud.

guardians.title: THE GUARDIANS GAZE
guardians.description: A subtle opening of the eyes raises the question: who is watching, who remembers, and who has been entrusted with care for the place.

voice.title: THE VOICE OF STORY
voice.description: A short narration can explain the meaning of Moai, Ahu and pukao without turning the space into a spectacle.

ahuLight.title: LIGHT BY THE AHU
ahuLight.description: Warm illumination does not advertise an attraction; it reveals the texture of stone, proportion and the gravity of the arrangement.

sign.title: A SIGN IN THE LANDSCAPE
sign.description: A discreet symbol leads onward and turns the passage through the Park into a reading of the landscape.

transformation.kicker: THE NIGHT CHAPTER OF THE AWAKENING
transformation.title: The Night of the Moai Awakening.
transformation.lead: This part focuses only on the night moment of the Awakening: the light of the eyes, darkness, stone and silence. Day and dusk remain described elsewhere in the section.
transformation.switcherAria: Choose a chapter of the Moai Awakening

rowBlue.title: The first blue across the line.
rowBlue.body: The night begins quietly. A cool rhythm of light appears along the Ahu, guiding the eye from the first Moai to the last without drowning out the stone.

closeBlue.title: A gaze seen up close.
closeBlue.body: Only in close view does the light stop feeling decorative. It reveals the features, fractures and weight of the face, as if the stone briefly answered the silence.

rowEmerald.title: Green as deep as night.
rowEmerald.body: The emerald tone changes the tension of the scene. It is not horror, but a second breath of the story: more mineral, darker, closer to the earth.

winterBlue.title: Guardians in winter darkness.
winterBlue.body: On snow, the light becomes even quieter. The white landscape does not soften the Moai; it strengthens their presence in the open space.

singleEmerald.title: A lone sign in the landscape.
singleEmerald.body: One Moai remains alone beneath a heavy sky. It is a pause in the narrative, a moment of focus before the final view.

gateBlue.title: The gate to the night finale.
gateBlue.body: The last image closes the chapter like an entrance to the Park after dark. Two monumental guardians lead the eye toward the distant illuminated line.

day.label: Day
day.name: DAY — GAZE
day.headline: By day, they watch.
day.body:
The Awakening begins in daylight.

On that day, the Moai of RapaNuiPark regain their eyes. A bright gaze contrasting with dark stone changes how we perceive the monumental figures.

For the first time, we do not only look at the Guardians.

We feel that they are looking at us.
day.detail: The eyes remain natural and calm. They do not glow. Their strength comes from how a small change can transform a stone face completely.

dusk.label: Dusk
dusk.name: DUSK — TRANSFORMATION
dusk.headline: The gaze begins to change.
dusk.body:
Then dusk arrives.

With the last light of day, the Awakening changes as well. Illumination begins to draw monumental silhouettes, facial lines and stone texture out of the half-dark.

The eyes that were bright and natural by day begin to reflect the light around them.
dusk.detail: The boundary between natural gaze and night experience slowly disappears. This is not full eye light yet, but a quiet passage.

night.label: Night
night.name: NIGHT — LIGHT OF THE EYES
night.headline: At night, their gaze becomes light.
night.body:
After dark, the Awakening reaches its finale.

Selected Moai eyes begin to glow with cool blue or deep emerald green. Not all at once.

First one gaze. Then another. Until the monumental row of Guardians becomes part of a night composition of light, stone and silence.
night.detail: The blue is deep and moonlit; the emerald is dark and mineral. The light stays subtle: no neon, no horror, no fairground rhythm.

summary.night: At night, their gaze becomes light.
summary.body: Moai Awakening lasts from the first gaze to the night finale.

ceremony.title: Opening of the Gaze
ceremony.description: The first chapter does not begin with noise, but with light. Faces slowly emerge from half-shadow, and the eyes of the Moai become the point around which the whole story takes shape.

trail.title: Path of Signs
trail.description: The walk through the Park leads through small traces: symbols, fragments of text, stone points and places to pause. It is a route for discovering rather than ticking off.

stories.title: Stories of the Ahu
stories.description: Each Ahu can have its own voice: about the placement of statues, the relation to landscape, ancestral memory and the meaning of looking toward the community.

feast.title: Hospitality of Place
feast.description: If food appears, it is part of the story of meeting, not the main product. It should build warmth, rest and respect for shared time.

photos.title: Frames of Memory
photos.description: Photography is not promotion here, but an attempt to capture a moment: gaze, stone texture, light and scale that stays with the visitor after leaving the Park.

symbols.title: Signs and Seals
symbols.description: A workshop can be a calm gesture: imprinting a symbol, making a mark, leaving a trace in memory. Understanding the motif matters more than the souvenir.

mystery.title: Hidden Story
mystery.description: Fragments of a larger story may appear in the terrain. They do not lead to a prize, but to the final meaning: why the guardians watch and what they guard.

light.title: Evening Silence
light.description: The last chapter should quiet the place. Light embraces the faces, the eyes remain open, and the Park becomes a landscape of memory, stone and night focus. During the finale of the Awakening, the Guardians' eyes become part of the illumination. Blue and emerald gazes appear between the light of the Ahu and the darkness of night.

timeline.title: One day. Five states of place.

dawn.title: First gaze
dawn.description: The beginning of the story and the slow opening of the eyes.

noon.title: Reading signs
noon.description: Paths, symbols and short stories guide visitors through the grounds.

afternoon.title: Memory and meeting
afternoon.description: Stories about Ahu, Moai, people and landscape.

dusk.title: Light of stone
dusk.description: Faces and textures revealed by calm illumination.

night.title: Silence of the guardians
night.description: The finale leaves the image of open eyes.

final.title: The guardians keep watching.
final.subtitle: The story does not end with dusk.
final.eventPending: The next chapter of the Awakening should grow from the rhythm of the Park and the maturity of the whole narrative.
final.announcedFallback: The next chapter of the Awakening has been announced.

lastLook.title: When night falls, the Guardians do not close their eyes.
lastLook.body: This is when the Awakening reaches its most extraordinary form. Light remains in the eyes of the Moai for a moment longer, before the exceptional day comes to an end.

story.title: It is not about an event. It is about what the place begins to say.
story.body: Moai Awakening should guide the visitor calmly: first through image, then through sign, then through story, and finally through a personal encounter with the monumental silence of the statues.

firstLook.title: First gaze
firstLook.body: The eyes of the Moai are not a special effect. They are a sign that the guardians have been noticed anew. From that moment, the visitor not only looks at the statues, but feels watched by them.

memory.title: Memory held in stone
memory.body: The story returns to Rapa Nui: to the work of hands, the weight of transport, the Ahu, and the communities that gave the statues meaning. The Awakening should remind us that Moai are not decoration, but carriers of memory.

path.title: Traces lead through the Park
path.body: Instead of intrusive attractions, discreet traces appear: a symbol on stone, light by the path, the voice of a guide, a short story written at a viewpoint. Each step reveals another fragment of the narrative.

evening.title: Evening closes the story
evening.body: As dusk falls, the Awakening turns into silence. Light does not create spectacle; it reveals faces, profiles and gazes. The finale should leave the memory of guardians who are still watching.

realizationStages.title: RapaNuiPark Realization Stages
realizationStages.subtitle: Three stages. One monumental vision.
realizationStages.body: RapaNuiPark has been conceived as a project developed in stages. Each successive phase expands what the place can offer, while preserving the value of everything built before it.

stage1.title: Foundation
stage1.lead: The spatial and symbolic core of RapaNuiPark takes shape.
stage1.body: The first phase of realization creates the basic spatial layout of RapaNuiPark and its most important monumental complexes. This is the stage that defines the scale, the character of the landscape and the recognizability of the entire undertaking.
stage1.planImageAlt: Stage I plan showing the basic spatial layout of RapaNuiPark.
stage1.planCaption: The first phase of realization sets the spatial and symbolic foundation of RapaNuiPark.

presentation.title: Discover the reference patterns
presentation.lead: See the authentic Rapa Nui places and forms that set the direction for the first phase of RapaNuiPark.
presentation.coverAlt: Cover of the RapaNuiPark Investment Stage I presentation.
presentation.openAria: Open the Investment Stage I presentation

stage2.title: The Place Comes Alive
stage2.body: The second phase expands the monumental foundation of RapaNuiPark with spaces that let visitors stay longer: discovery, education, events, dining, observation, gatherings and rest.

amphitheater.title: Rapa Nui Amphitheatre
amphitheater.alt: Concept of the Rapa Nui Amphitheatre in the second phase of RapaNuiPark.
amphitheater.body: An intimate space for events, storytelling and evening gatherings. The Amphitheatre is designed to host presentations, chamber concerts, screenings, educational meetings and artistic programs related to Rapa Nui culture.

model.title: Rapa Nui at a Single Glance
model.subtitle: A monumental scale model of the island
model.alt: Monumental scale model of Rapa Nui island as an educational attraction of RapaNuiPark.
model.body: A spatial scale model lets visitors see Rapa Nui as a whole: its volcanoes, coastline, the most important Ahu, historic sites, and the relationship between landscape and culture.

discoveryCenter.title: Discovery Center — Te Tokanga
discoveryCenter.subtitle: An archaeological site as the heart of the story.
discoveryCenter.alt: Discovery Center with a reclining Te Tokanga presented as part of the archaeological site.
discoveryCenter.body: The Discovery Center takes visitors into the world of archaeology and research on the monumental Moai. At its center lies a reclining Te Tokanga, presented as part of the archaeological site.

viewTower.title: Moai Viewing Tower
viewTower.subtitle: RapaNuiPark from a completely different perspective.
viewTower.alt: Concept of the Moai Viewing Tower with an observation platform and Sky Café.
viewTower.body: A monumental tower inspired by the form of a Moai is set to become one of RapaNuiPark's most recognizable landmarks. The Sky Café sits at the tower's viewing level.

pavilion.title: Rapa Nui Pavilion
pavilion.subtitle: The heart of life at RapaNuiPark.
pavilion.alt: Concept board of the Rapa Nui Pavilion with a museum, restaurant, gallery, Visitor Center and pathways.
pavilion.body: A low, ring-shaped pavilion is designed to bring together the Rapa Nui Museum, the Rapa Nui Restaurant, the RapaNuiPark Gallery and the Visitor Center. Paths and landscaping tie the attractions into a single visiting route.

closing.title: The place comes alive.
closing.body: The second phase gives the monumental space functions that let visitors experience RapaNuiPark for hours at a time — discovering, observing, resting, taking part in events, and returning at different times of day and year.

stage3.title: Full Vision
stage3.body: The third phase will expand RapaNuiPark to its full intended scale. The detailed scope of this part of the project will be presented at a later stage of development.
